newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols sharply lower post-data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols sharply lower post-data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt futures options dropped sharply as the market heaved a sigh of relief following the release of benign U.S. economic data on Friday morning.
Implied volatility for December T-bond options fell 0.60 percentage point to 9.90 percent after the release of producer price and retail sales data for September, dealers said.
Implied volatility for March T-bonds fell 0.25 percentage point to 9.60 percent, they said.
T-bond futures rallied sharply after the data, which held few surprises.
Dealers at the Chicago Board of Trade noted heavy call buying before the data with one house, in particular, buying 6000 November 112-00, 111-00 and 109-00 calls.
Despite the slide in volatilities, Brad Tyl, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston, cautioned that the market remains vulnerable to comments by Federal Reserve officials.

He cited last Friday's rally in bond futures as a case in point. December T-bond futures soared after on weak employment growth but then erased much of those gains on Wednesday, when Fed governor Lawrence Lindsey said higher rates may be necessary to curb inflation.
Implied volatilities for March and June eurodollar futures options were flat at 15.8 percent and 18.2 percent respectively but expected to drop by day's end.
Volatilities from September 1997 and out were up slightly but expected to slip back to neutral by the U.S. close.
"We have a three day weekend. I think they'll take some of the weekend premium out and we should finish a little lower," one CME dealer said.
He added that this slide will be limited by the shadow of upcoming U.S. consumer price and industrial production data, which could have a significant impact on the market.

Implied volatilities for short-dated eurodollar options were also sharply lower at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, dealers said. At 945 CDT/1445 GMT, implied volatility for December euro options was down 0.75 percent at 10.55 percent while November at-the-money options were down 1.75 percent at 9.36 percent.

"It's not surprising with the confirmation of the trading range that December on in is lower," one CME dealer said. "And bear in mind, October goes off the board today, which naturally puts some offer into December and November."

The Chicago Board of Trade's financial and insurance contracts will close early at 1210 CDT/1710 GMT on Friday and will remain closed on Monday. The CME will observe normal trading hours on Friday but will close all contracts at noon on Monday, with the exception of the Goldman Sachs Commodity Index and equity index products.
